evidence.claim: The President holds executive power, may submit bills, issue implementing regulations, and is assisted by a Vice-President and ministers whom the President appoints and dismisses.
evidence.title: Indonesia 1945 (reinst. 1959, rev. 2002) Constitution
evidence.excerpt: The President holds executive power, may submit bills, issue implementing regulations, and is assisted by a Vice-President and ministers whom the President appoints and dismisses.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Constitutional text directly states executive authority and cabinet appointment/removal powers.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct institutional authority; these powers belong to the Indonesian presidency, not to Jokowi personally alone.
contrary_evidence: Legislative bargaining and coalition politics can constrain how much of this authority is usable in practice.

evidence.claim: The World Bank approved a $350 million loan to support Indonesia’s human capital agenda by safeguarding income protection, increasing access to healthcare services, preventing unhealthy behavior, and improving the effectiveness of government spending.
evidence.title: New Financing Will Support Indonesia to Improve and Protect Human Capital
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank approved a $350 million loan to support Indonesia’s human capital agenda by safeguarding income protection, increasing access to healthcare services, preventing unhealthy behavior, and improving the effectiveness of government spending.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official World Bank press release with a specific approval, policy purpose, and implementation framing for Indonesia.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in period; published in July 2022 and describes 2022 policy action.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to Jokowi’s administration and policy agenda, but the financing is a World Bank instrument and not solely personal presidential action.
contrary_evidence: The same source says Indonesia’s human capital score still lagged the East Asia and Pacific average and that weaknesses remained in education and social insurance.

evidence.claim: Indonesia’s Human Capital Index improved from 0.50 to 0.54 between 2010 and 2020, but remained below East Asia and Pacific peers because of weaknesses in education, social insurance, and a relatively high stunting rate.
evidence.title: New Financing Will Support Indonesia to Improve and Protect Human Capital
evidence.excerpt: Indonesia’s Human Capital Index improved from 0.50 to 0.54 between 2010 and 2020, but remained below East Asia and Pacific peers because of weaknesses in education, social insurance, and a relatively high stunting rate.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official World Bank statement using a concrete trend metric and explicit diagnostic explanation.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective baseline context used for the 2022 ruler-period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly inherited trajectory and sectoral baseline; only partial attribution to Jokowi’s 2022 choices.
contrary_evidence: The same source frames the improvement as partial and still below regional averages.

evidence.claim: Indonesia had made remarkable poverty reduction progress and had essentially eradicated extreme poverty by 2022, with previously lagging regions catching up.
evidence.title: Indonesia Poverty Assessment: Pathways Towards Economic Security
evidence.excerpt: Indonesia had made remarkable poverty reduction progress and had essentially eradicated extreme poverty by 2022, with previously lagging regions catching up.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official World Bank assessment summarizing 2022 poverty outcomes with clear quantitative and qualitative framing.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to Jokowi-era policy mix, but also to long-run growth and preexisting regional convergence.
contrary_evidence: The same report says significant non-extreme poverty and insecurity remained, so the achievement was incomplete.

evidence.claim: More than one-third of Indonesians remained economically insecure in 2022 and could be pushed into poverty by shocks such as COVID-19 or natural disasters.
evidence.title: Indonesia Poverty Assessment: Pathways Towards Economic Security
evidence.excerpt: More than one-third of Indonesians remained economically insecure in 2022 and could be pushed into poverty by shocks such as COVID-19 or natural disasters.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official assessment with a direct, plainly stated estimate and risk characterization.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Only partly attributable to the ruler; reflects structural vulnerability, labor-market structure, and external shocks.
contrary_evidence: The same source notes social assistance and resilience investments can mitigate these risks, so the problem is not total policy failure.

evidence.claim: Indonesia’s poverty rate in September 2022 was 9.57 percent, with 26.36 million poor people; urban poverty was 7.53 percent and rural poverty was 12.36 percent.
evidence.title: Persentase Penduduk Miskin September 2022 naik menjadi 9,57 persen
evidence.excerpt: Indonesia’s poverty rate in September 2022 was 9.57 percent, with 26.36 million poor people; urban poverty was 7.53 percent and rural poverty was 12.36 percent.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official national statistics release with direct 2022 headline numbers and urban-rural breakdown.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 measurement published soon after the period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Country-level outcome with partial attribution to national policy; not all movement is ruler-specific.
contrary_evidence: Poverty was still materially present and rural poverty remained much higher than urban poverty.

evidence.claim: Indonesia’s HDI in 2022 reached 72.91, up 0.62 points from 2021; life expectancy, education, and decent living standards all improved.
evidence.title: Indeks Pembangunan Manusia (IPM) Indonesia tahun 2022 mencapai 72,91
evidence.excerpt: Indonesia’s HDI in 2022 reached 72.91, up 0.62 points from 2021; life expectancy, education, and decent living standards all improved.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official BPS release with direct annual HDI change and component trends.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Broad national outcome with some attribution to Jokowi’s policy environment, but also to inherited baseline and demography.
contrary_evidence: The improvement was incremental rather than transformative.

evidence.claim: Extended school closures and disrupted reopenings affected around 60 million students and caused significant learning loss, with harms especially acute for low-income, rural, disadvantaged, and disabled children.
evidence.title: As children in Indonesia return to school, UNICEF calls for urgent action to address learning crisis
evidence.excerpt: Extended school closures and disrupted reopenings affected around 60 million students and caused significant learning loss, with harms especially acute for low-income, rural, disadvantaged, and disabled children.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UNICEF press release citing concrete scale and distribution of educational harm in Indonesia.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and describing the post-pandemic recovery environment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to the government’s education recovery response; the underlying disruption was inherited from COVID-19.
contrary_evidence: The same source frames the issue as a learning crisis rather than a complete collapse of access.

evidence.claim: Indonesia made substantial progress in improved drinking water, sanitation, and basic hygiene, but safely managed WASH access remained low, and girls faced disproportionate health and education burdens where WASH facilities were unsafe or absent.
evidence.title: WASH Acts – 2022 Edition
evidence.excerpt: Indonesia made substantial progress in improved drinking water, sanitation, and basic hygiene, but safely managed WASH access remained low, and girls faced disproportionate health and education burdens where WASH facilities were unsafe or absent.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UNICEF summary page describing Indonesia-specific WASH conditions and policy work in 2022.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 frame with contemporaneous program context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to government and partner policy; also reflects long-run infrastructure and geography constraints.
contrary_evidence: The source emphasizes that progress exists but safe service coverage remains low.

evidence.claim: In 2022 Indonesia achieved 94.6 percent full immunization coverage, exceeding the national target of 94.1 percent, and the BIAN catch-up campaign reached 26.5 million children with measles-rubella vaccines.
evidence.title: Indonesia Targets Low Vaccination Areas to Tackle Decline in Childhood Immunization
evidence.excerpt: In 2022 Indonesia achieved 94.6 percent full immunization coverage, exceeding the national target of 94.1 percent, and the BIAN catch-up campaign reached 26.5 million children with measles-rubella vaccines.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: WHO country office release with specific national coverage and campaign-reach numbers.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective evidence about 2022 immunization outcomes and campaign response.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the health ministry and national government response under Jokowi, though implementation was shared with subnational systems.
contrary_evidence: The same release says there were still low-coverage areas and recent outbreaks of vaccine-preventable disease.

evidence.claim: Indonesia’s stunting rate fell by 2.8 percentage points from 2021 to 2022, and the ministry said this was in line with the annual pace needed to reach the 14 percent target by 2024.
evidence.title: Kementerian Kesehatan Rilis Hasil Survei Status Gizi Indonesia (SSGI) tahun 2022
evidence.excerpt: Indonesia’s stunting rate fell by 2.8 percentage points from 2021 to 2022, and the ministry said this was in line with the annual pace needed to reach the 14 percent target by 2024.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official ministry release summarizing the national SSGI 2022 result; precise percentages are explicit even though the page is narrative rather than tabular.
evidence.period_fit: Directly about 2022 results, published shortly after the measurement year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to national health policy under Jokowi, but also influenced by nutrition, provincial delivery, and household factors.
contrary_evidence: The source still shows stunting remained high enough that the 2024 target required faster progress.

evidence.claim: Jokowi issued Inpres 4/2022 to accelerate elimination of extreme poverty by 2024 through integrated, targeted coordination across ministries and local governments, including education aid, health access, stunting reduction, sanitation, PBI JKN enrollment, clean water, housing, and data targeting.
evidence.title: Presiden Jokowi Keluarkan Inpres 4/2022 tentang Percepatan Penghapusan Kemiskinan Ekstrem
evidence.excerpt: Jokowi issued Inpres 4/2022 to accelerate elimination of extreme poverty by 2024 through integrated, targeted coordination across ministries and local governments, including education aid, health access, stunting reduction, sanitation, PBI JKN enrollment, clean water, housing, and data targeting.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential instruction text reproduced by the cabinet secretariat with detailed ministry tasks and dates.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to Jokowi personally as the issuing president and direct commander of the relevant ministries.
contrary_evidence: Implementation still depended on ministries and local governments; the instruction itself does not prove delivery quality.

evidence.claim: Jokowi said more than 70 percent of fuel subsidies were benefiting better-off car owners and announced reallocation to targeted support, including BLT BBM for 20.65 million poor families and wage subsidies for 16 million workers.
evidence.title: Pernyataan Pers Presiden RI mengenai Pengalihan Subsidi BBM
evidence.excerpt: Jokowi said more than 70 percent of fuel subsidies were benefiting better-off car owners and announced reallocation to targeted support, including BLT BBM for 20.65 million poor families and wage subsidies for 16 million workers.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential statement with specific budget and beneficiary counts.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to Jokowi because he announced and justified the reallocation himself.
contrary_evidence: The move was a response to inflationary pressure and fiscal burden, not a clean prosperity windfall.

evidence.claim: By late October 2022, BLT BBM disbursement had reached 99.7 percent and wage-subsidy disbursement had reached 72 percent, with Jokowi framing the assistance as a way to preserve purchasing power and even support child nutrition.
evidence.title: Presiden Jokowi Serahkan Bantuan Sosial di Balikpapan
evidence.excerpt: By late October 2022, BLT BBM disbursement had reached 99.7 percent and wage-subsidy disbursement had reached 72 percent, with Jokowi framing the assistance as a way to preserve purchasing power and even support child nutrition.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct cabinet-secretariat report of presidential remarks and delivery progress with concrete percentages.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and tied to rollout of the fuel-subsidy reallocation package.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to Jokowi because the report describes his own remarks and supervision of disbursement.
contrary_evidence: The source itself links the aid to a costly subsidy reallocation rather than to a structural welfare reform.

evidence.claim: Jokowi oversaw targeted social assistance in Nias for children, the elderly, and persons with disabilities, including ATENSI, PKH, BLT Minyak Goreng, and Sembako, with assistive devices and small-business capital support.
evidence.title: Pesan Presiden Jokowi: Bantuan yang Diberikan untuk Menambah Modal Usaha
evidence.excerpt: Jokowi oversaw targeted social assistance in Nias for children, the elderly, and persons with disabilities, including ATENSI, PKH, BLT Minyak Goreng, and Sembako, with assistive devices and small-business capital support.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official ministry report with specific beneficiary groups, package types, and monetary totals, though written as a news item rather than an audited delivery record.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to Jokowi as the president present at and endorsing the targeted distribution.
contrary_evidence: The report is a single-event example, not nationwide proof of fairness or coverage.

evidence.claim: Regsosek was a nationwide socioeconomic registration covering housing, clean water sanitation, asset ownership, vulnerability of special groups, geospatial information, and welfare levels, intended to rank welfare and improve government intervention effectiveness.
evidence.title: Initial Registration of Regsosek Begins
evidence.excerpt: Regsosek was a nationwide socioeconomic registration covering housing, clean water sanitation, asset ownership, vulnerability of special groups, geospatial information, and welfare levels, intended to rank welfare and improve government intervention effectiveness.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official BPS news release describing a concrete nationwide data system and its intended use.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the national government and BPS under Jokowi’s administration, though operational execution was statistical rather than personal presidential action.
contrary_evidence: The page explains the system design, not the quality of subsequent targeting or outcomes.

evidence.claim: The social-assistance registry uses DTSEN/desil targeting; desil 1-4 can be proposed for PKH and Sembako, and desil 5 can be proposed for PBI-JK, with the classification being dynamic and updateable through local verification.
evidence.title: Cek Bansos Kemensos
evidence.excerpt: The social-assistance registry uses DTSEN/desil targeting; desil 1-4 can be proposed for PKH and Sembako, and desil 5 can be proposed for PBI-JK, with the classification being dynamic and updateable through local verification.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official live government eligibility portal that clearly states targeting rules, though it is not a dated report.
evidence.period_fit: Current system page describing the targeting architecture used in 2022-era social protection delivery.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government system under Jokowi; the portal is institutional rather than personally authored by him.
contrary_evidence: Because it is a live registry page, it establishes rules and architecture more than verified 2022 delivery performance.

evidence.claim: PMK 134/PMK.07/2022 required local governments to budget social-protection spending for October to December 2022, including assistance for ojek, UMKM, and fishers, to respond to inflation.
evidence.title: 134/PMK.07/2022 - Belanja Wajib dalam rangka Penanganan Dampak Inflasi Tahun Anggaran 2022
evidence.excerpt: PMK 134/PMK.07/2022 required local governments to budget social-protection spending for October to December 2022, including assistance for ojek, UMKM, and fishers, to respond to inflation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official legal summary of a specific 2022 regulation with direct welfare spending obligations and target groups.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Jokowi administration through the Ministry of Finance’s regulatory response, though implementation was decentralized.
contrary_evidence: The rule is crisis-response spending, not a durable welfare expansion.

evidence.claim: To avoid pushing more families into economic precarity, the government increased its social-protection budget by IDR 5.6 trillion, and the second 2022 survey focused on children and other vulnerable groups.
evidence.title: The social and economic impact of COVID-19 on households in Indonesia
evidence.excerpt: To avoid pushing more families into economic precarity, the government increased its social-protection budget by IDR 5.6 trillion, and the second 2022 survey focused on children and other vulnerable groups.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UNICEF report with specific budget and survey details, produced with UNDP and Indonesian research partners.
evidence.period_fit: Directly about the 2022 household situation and 2022 survey round.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Indonesian government’s pandemic-response and recovery policy mix under Jokowi, but the shock itself was inherited from COVID-19.
contrary_evidence: The report highlights that households were still coping with serious precarity two years into the pandemic.
